correctness.rationale: For each character of the unit squares modulo \(p^2\), the principal-unit sum is exactly p times a stationary fiber indexed by \(x-x^{-1}\) in the residue-field square subgroup. Two-point fibers cannot cancel since their phase ratio has primitive \(p^2\)-order while tame character ratios have order coprime to p; singleton fibers contribute modulus p. Counting orbits of \(x\mapsto-x^{-1}\) proves all three rank cases and the p-flat positive spectrum when \(p\equiv3\pmod4\). The checker reproduced direct matrix ranks at primes 3,5,7,11,13 under c=1,2 and exact fiber counts up to 41.
